title: 1985 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Find the least positive integer \(n\) for which \(\frac{n-13}{5n+6}\) is a non-zero reducible fraction.

solutions.text:
Euclid’s algorithm gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\gcd(n-13,5n+6)\\ &\quad=\gcd(n-13,71). \end{aligned} \] Since \(71\) is prime, the nonzero fraction is reducible exactly when \(n-13\) is a nonzero multiple of \(71.\) The least positive possibility is \(n=13+71=84,\) which is not among the four numerical choices.

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Any common divisor of \(n-13\) and \(5n+6\) also divides a suitable linear combination
